problems: All five dossiers validate (0 errors, 0 warnings, also with --resolve). 21 distinct pages were opened (Idrisid dynasty, Idris I, Idris II, Emirate of Nekor, Tlemcen, Aghlabids, Muslim conquest of Sicily, Emirate of Bari, Rustamid dynasty, Tulunids, Hammadid dynasty, Qal'at Bani Hammad, Banu Hilal, Bejaia, Zirid dynasty, Kingdom of Africa, Almoravid dynasty, Yusuf ibn Tashfin, Banu Ghaniya, Almohad Caliphate, Takrur); sources_total counts a page once per dossier that cites it. The Almoravid page was opened twice (second time for the Andalusian sentences). Page budgets respected; the Hammadid, Almoravid and Zirid dossiers also cite pages opened for their neighbours.
WebFetch returns a model-made extraction, so quoted phrases may differ slightly from the live text; each dossier's notes say so.

Zirid dossier starts 972 (page: Established 972) against Cliopatria's 1056, so its 972-1055 keyframes overlap the Fatimid Caliphate shapes 970-1055, which contain Ifriqiya: the Fatimid dossier (me-08) must draw Zirid Ifriqiya as viceroyalty or client, or one of the two must cede the cells.

Aghlabid dossier uses Cliopatria's Emirate of Sicily shapes (850-910) for Sicily; the Emirate of Sicily dossier (eu-13) should treat the island as Aghlabid land until 25 March 909 or the same cells are claimed twice. Cliopatria's Aghlabid 900-910 shape has lost Sicily.

Almoravid dossier ends 1203, not 1147: the Balearic Banu Ghaniya, 'a branch of the Almoravids', are kept as one state with a rename event in 1147, as Cliopatria's row (to 1205) does; the reviewer may prefer to split 1148-1203 into a dossier banu-ghaniya.

Hammadid dossier ends 1152 (Yahya's surrender 10 November 1152) against Cliopatria's 1151; Idrisids end 974 against Cliopatria's 979; Aghlabids end 25 March 909 against 910; Zirids 12 July 1148 against 1151.

Cliopatria's Hammadid shape from 1066 (32,800 km2) lacks the capital Qal'at Bani Hammad until 1090; keyframes 1066, 1072b and 1082 replace it. Cliopatria's Idrisid shapes 947 and 970 are marked wrong (the family held only northern Morocco after 927).

Several keyframes reuse the neighbours' Cliopatria shapes (Barghawata Conference, Emirate of Nekor, Taifa rows, Emirate of Sicily, Hammadid Dynasty, Rustamid dynasty); if their dossiers re-time those shapes, the unions here need re-checking.
